findings.summary: Two unrelated interfaces named 'FileChange' exist in different modules with different shapes, both re-exported from barrel files
evidence: src/vcs/types.ts:154 defines FileChange with { path: string; content: string | null }
src/output/sync-report.ts:20 defines FileChange with { path: string; action: 'create' | 'update' | 'delete' }
Both are re-exported from their respective barrel files (vcs/index.ts, output/index.ts)
findings.suggestion: Rename one or both to disambiguate: e.g. VcsFileChange (content-bearing) vs ReportFileChange (action-only), or consolidate into a single shared type

findings.summary: Four closely related types represent file changes with overlapping but slightly different shapes, creating confusion about which to use where
evidence: vcs/types.ts: FileChange { path, content } - for commit payloads
vcs/pr-creator.ts: FileAction { fileName, action } - for PR descriptions
sync/types.ts: FileChangeDetail { path, action } - for processor results
output/sync-report.ts: FileChange { path, action } - for report output
FileChangeDetail and output/FileChange have identical shapes but different names
FileAction uses 'fileName' while others use 'path' for the same concept
findings.suggestion: Consolidate FileChangeDetail and output/FileChange into a single type. Standardize the field name (path vs fileName) across FileAction and related types.

findings.summary: sync/types.ts imports FileAction from the concrete vcs/pr-creator.ts rather than from vcs/types.ts or vcs/index.ts barrel
evidence: sync/types.ts:9 - import type { FileAction } from '../vcs/pr-creator.js'
sync/file-sync-orchestrator.ts:4 - import type { FileAction } from '../vcs/pr-creator.js'
sync/commit-message.ts:1 - import type { FileAction } from '../vcs/pr-creator.js'
FileAction is not exported from vcs/index.ts or vcs/types.ts, forcing direct file imports that bypass the barrel
findings.suggestion: Move FileAction to vcs/types.ts and export it from vcs/index.ts. This keeps cross-module imports going through the barrel.

findings.summary: The three settings processors return slightly different result shapes despite sharing a base type, with inconsistent presence of optional fields
evidence: RulesetProcessorResult has { changes?, planOutput?: RulesetPlanResult }
LabelsProcessorResult has { changes?, planOutput?: LabelsPlanResult }
RepoSettingsProcessorResult has { changes?, warnings?, planOutput?: RepoSettingsPlanResult }
Only RepoSettingsProcessorResult has 'warnings' at the result level, though the base-processor's buildDryRunResult supports passing arbitrary extra fields
The consuming code in sync-command.ts logSettingsResult checks result.warnings and result.planOutput?.lines generically, meaning it expects a uniform shape but gets different types
findings.suggestion: Add 'warnings' to BaseProcessorResult (optional) so all three result types consistently support it, or define a common SettingsProcessorResult that includes warnings.

findings.summary: gh-api-utils.ts in shared/ contains both low-level API utilities (GhApiClient, parseApiJson) and a high-level token resolution function (resolveGitHubToken) that understands GitHub App installation semantics
evidence: GhApiClient is a stateful class wrapping executor+retries for GitHub API calls
resolveGitHubToken() handles GitHub App token resolution with fallback to GH_TOKEN env
parseApiJson() is a JSON parser with domain-specific error wrapping (throws GraphQLApiError)
isHttp404Error() is a simple string-match utility
These span two abstraction levels: infrastructure (API client, JSON parsing) and business logic (token resolution strategy with App installation awareness)
findings.suggestion: Consider splitting: keep GhApiClient/parseApiJson/buildTokenEnv/getHostnameFlag/isHttp404Error as API infrastructure utilities, and move resolveGitHubToken to a more domain-specific location (e.g., vcs/ or a dedicated auth module)

findings.summary: cli/types.ts re-exports types from other modules (IRepositoryProcessor, IRulesetProcessor, IRepoSettingsProcessor, ILabelsProcessor) alongside its own definitions, creating ambiguous import sources
evidence: cli/types.ts:3 imports IRepositoryProcessor from sync/index.ts
cli/types.ts:8 imports ISettingsProcessor, IRulesetProcessor, IRepoSettingsProcessor, ILabelsProcessor from settings/index.ts
cli/types.ts:13 re-exports: export type { IRepositoryProcessor, IRulesetProcessor }
cli/types.ts:92 re-exports: export type { IRepoSettingsProcessor, ILabelsProcessor }
cli/index.ts:3-10 re-exports these same types from cli/types.ts, adding a third layer
Consumers can import IRepositoryProcessor from sync/index, cli/types, or cli/index
findings.suggestion: Remove re-exports from cli/types.ts and cli/index.ts. Let consumers import these interfaces directly from their owning modules (sync/ and settings/).

findings.summary: RepositoryProcessor constructor uses logger singleton as default when no ILogger is passed, which weakens the DI pattern by making the singleton accessible from library code
evidence: repository-processor.ts:6 imports { logger, ILogger } from '../shared/logger.js'
repository-processor.ts:58 uses: const logInstance = log ?? logger

This means RepositoryProcessor (library code in sync/) has a direct import of the logger singleton, which CLAUDE.md says should be avoided: 'Only CLI entry points and composition roots may import singletons directly'
findings.suggestion: Remove the logger singleton import. Make the ILogger parameter required, or have the composition root (cli/sync-command.ts) always pass it explicitly. The RepositoryProcessor is already only instantiated from sync-command.ts.
